title: "Revert and Unmerge"
---

# `git revert` and Unmerging Changes

After this page you can undo a **published** commit by adding a new commit, including a merge.

## Revert writes history forward

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git switch main
git revert HEAD --no-edit
git log --oneline -3
```

The bad commit is still in the graph. A new commit applies the inverse patch. Shared clones can fast-forward. This is the safe undo on `main`.

```text
 reset --hard HEAD~1     (local only)     A ← B            main
                                          C still in reflog

 revert HEAD             (shared)         A ← B ← C ← R    main
                                          R undoes C; C remains
```

`--no-edit` keeps Git’s default message (`Revert "…"`). Edit with `git revert HEAD` if you need a `fix:` subject.

## Several commits

```bash
git revert --no-edit HEAD~2..HEAD
```

Reverts newest first (the range is exclusive on the left). Conflicts: `git add` and `git revert --continue`, or `git revert --abort`.

## Revert a merge commit

A merge has two parents. Git needs to know which parent is “the mainline” to diff against:

```bash
git revert -m 1 <merge-hash>
```

`-m 1` means “keep first parent’s tree; undo what the merged branch brought in.” `-m 2` is the other parent (almost never what you want on `main`).

After reverting a merge, Git considers that feature’s commits **already merged**. Cherry-picking them back later can no-op. To re-land the feature, revert the revert, or rebase the feature into new hashes.

## Revert vs reset vs restore

| Goal | Command | History |
|------|---------|---------|
| Throw away uncommitted edits | `git restore` | Unchanged |
| Replace last unpublished commit | `git commit --amend` / `reset` | Rewritten |
| Undo a published commit | `git revert` | New commit |

`git reset --hard` on shared `main` is a force-push incident. Revert instead.

## Un-merge without `-m`

If the merge was never pushed and is `HEAD`:

```bash
git reset --hard HEAD~1
```

That moves `main` to first parent and drops the merge commit from the branch name. Only on a lab clone or an unpublished branch. Chapter 7 is reset in full. The merge commit stays in the reflog (chapter 17) until it expires.
